questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had already been to Colombia and loved it, so when I had to choose a destination it made sense for me to apply there. I also wanted to improve my spanish

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Colombia is an amazing country and apart from the academic opportunities, you also get the chance to travel a lot within the country which was a big part of my exchange experience as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, they send you a lot of emails with information (which at times was a bit overwhelming, however helpful) and there is a group of students who greet you the first week - they are super helpful throughout the semester as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The group of Colombian students and the exchange office provide assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: For me everything was fine, but it can feel a bit chaotic in the beginning.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in CentralX18 which is very close to uni, and it was quite easy to apply for - just write them on whatsapp.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everyone lives off campus - a lot of the exchange students live in candelaria so if you only stay one semester, I would recommend living there since it is also super close to uni. However, it is not the safest neighborhood there is, so if you are very concerned about that (I wouldn't be though) then maybe go more north in the city. Bogotá is huge so just be aware that transportation can be longer than you'd expect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university has an agreement with CityU (also student housing) which is also right next to campus, but if you want to live in that area, then CentralX is much better - rooms are bigger and it is a bit cheaper as well. Just a heads up:)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To be honest, it was super confusing....

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to register for courses in different platforms and it is best to do it before you go there, if you want to make sure you get the classes you want. They send you a website where you see all the different courses that each have a registration number that you have to apply for in 2 different platforms. It's frustrating, but hang in there

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always write to the international office, or get help from the tutors once you arrive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. And try to do it in advance if you can to make sure you get the classes you want. You can also take more classes than you need, and then drop them later in the semester. They have a lof of fun classes - I took ceramics and loved it, so if you have the patience really try and look throught all the courses. Most of them are in spanish but there are also some english ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level depends a lot on the professor. I had one class which was quit difficult, but that I really liked. And then I had one which felt a bit like high school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is quite different because you are in a classroom - the classes feel more like the seminars we have at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contextos de America Latina y Colombia 
Psicologia social critica 
Ceramica

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved all my classes - especially critical social psychology which is not only for psychology students but uses literature from all the social sciences. You learn a lot about Colombia and latinamerica in general. It is taught in Spanish so I was the only exchange student in the class, but it worked out well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The flight was very expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general it is not expensive compared to Copenhagen. But do take into account that you'll eat out and go out a lot so it adds up. But that's also part of the experience.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have all kinds of clubs and sports and it's free

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The salsa classes and ceramics

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There is so much to see in Colombia, and people travel a lot. I would recommend staying in Colombia and not going to other countries because time flies and there is already a lot to see. Go to the caribbean coast, Cali and the amazon if you can! 
Also spend some time in getting to know Bogotá. It has a lot to offer even though it might not seem like in in the beginning.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had already been there and spoke spanish quite well which made it easier. It did however take me some time to adjust to Bogotá because it is such a big city that at times can seem a bit grey. A lot of people will tell you that Colombia is super unsafe before you go, and although nothing ever happened to me and there is many more good things to say about the country, you do have to be aware of your surroundings more than you're used to in Denmark (surprise;) which did take me some time to get used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just approach them, they are very nice:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The security issue

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is very open and helpful

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient - things might take longer than in Denmark 
Be open to trying new things
Don't do coke:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You do not have to speak fluent Spanish to go there - a lot of exchange students don't

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people you meet

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time management hehe;) The semester goes by quickly and you want to make the most of it - so prioritize your time, but also just chill and have fun

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
